title: weight-decay-induced-misrouting-root-cause-and-temporary-mitigations
creator: Lina Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-02-18 we observed a multi-region surge of fallback traffic following an automated weight-decay pass in the routing controller. Instead of smoothly rebalancing load, the decay step caused a rapid demotion of a small set of healthy tier-1 pools in eu-west-1. That demotion combined with stale tombstone reconciliation and a TTL skew in the control plane caused a cascade of misroutes to lower-cost model variants and a 3x increase in end-to-end p95 latency for affected customers. This ticket contains the investigation notes, immediate mitigations we applied, and proposed long-term fixes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate weight-decay job against current routing weights in staging with artificially short grace periods. 2) Patch control plane to add 30s delay on tombstone reconciliation to mirror production. 3) Replay traffic profile from 2026-02-18 on staging and observe tier demotions and fallback activations. 4) Measure KV cache warmup and cold-start latency on fallback variants.
root_cause: Three contributing factors combined to amplify a small scheduled change into a large outage: 1) aggressive weight-decay configuration: the decay job reduced weights for pools with minor error rate blips by 60% within a single pass. 2) control-plane TTL drift: the routing TTL published by edge agents lagged controller state by up to 45s due to sequential reconciliation windows, causing clients to continue routing to demoted pools which then triggered rapid evictions and rebalancing. 3) stale tombstones and slow reconciliation: nodes marked for soft-drain produced stale tombstones that were not reconciled until the next daily compaction job, leaving compatibility hashes mismatched and causing many requests to be considered incompatible with the preferred variant, forcing fallbacks.
timeline:
2026-02-18 03:12 UTC: weight-decay job started.
2026-02-18 03:14 UTC: first customer reports of elevated latency in eu-west-1.
2026-02-18 03:18 UTC: routing controller logs show >50% weight drops for 7 pools.
2026-02-18 03:22 UTC: automated fallback policy engaged en masse to lower-capacity variants.
2026-02-18 03:30 UTC: on-call notified; initial mitigation toggles applied (soft rollback of decay).
2026-02-18 04:05 UTC: control-plane TTL resync script executed, improving routing convergence.
2026-02-18 04:30 UTC: tombstone reconciliation job kickstarted manually, compatibility hashes reconciled.
2026-02-18 05:10 UTC: metrics returned to baseline for most customers; partial residuals until KV caches warmed (next 90 minutes).
immediate_mitigations: 1) Rolled back that night's weight-decay pass and disabled automated runs until config reviewed. 2) Extended the grace window for pool demotion from 60s to 300s to prevent one-pass 60% demotions. 3) Deployed a temporary control-plane TTL override to force a full resync across edge agents. 4) Manually triggered tombstone compaction and compatibility-hash reconciliation. 5) Opened a hotfix PR to add a circuit-breaker that prevents >30% weight change for any single pool in a single job run.
monitoring_and_metrics:
- Peak fallback traffic increase: 320% on eu-west-1 for variants with lower capacity.
- Customer-facing p95 latency: increased from 180ms to 580ms for affected routes.
- Error rate: 0.8% increase in 4xx/5xx during the peak window.
- Time to partial recovery after mitigations: ~50 minutes; full KV cache warmup ~90 minutes.
Dashboards updated: routing-controller/decay-run-heatmap, regional-fallbacks/eu-west-1, kv-cache-warmup-trace.
long_term_fixes: 1) Change weight-decay algorithm to a multi-pass gradual decay with per-pool adaptive thresholds and a max-per-pass delta of 15%. 2) Implement an authoritative tombstone reconciliation microjob that runs on weight-decay completion and reconciles compatibility hashes within 10s. 3) Add a controller-side canary window for any routing weight change: begin with 1% of traffic and advance only after safety checks. 4) Rework control-plane TTL propagation to use event-driven push for critical routing changes instead of periodic pulls. 5) Add an automated smoke test that replays 10m of representative traffic after any routing-change job before it is promoted to production. 6) Document new operational runbook for routing decay incidents and create an on-call checklist.
postmortem_actions:
- PR #7491: add circuit-breaker to decay job (author: Marco Ruiz).
- RFC-220: propose event-driven TTL and reconciliation (author: Lina Chen).
- ENG-56890: follow-up to implement multi-pass decay algorithm (dependency).
- QA ticket QAL-102: add synthetic replay tests to CI.
- Runbook created and published to Confluence: /confluence/teams/routing/postmortem-ENG-54321.
owner_notes: We intentionally left the decay job enabled for non-critical regions to gather telemetry on the multi-pass proposal. The emergency rollback validated that the decay job is the primary trigger but the TTL/reconciliation problems significantly amplified the effect. Consider deprioritizing any global automated soft-drain mechanisms until reconciliation latencies < 10s.
